# Onam

> Onam (https://www.onamsecurity.com) is Onam Security — cloud security, SaaS security and code security on one
> security graph — with Onam AI, an AI security analyst (early access). Onam Estate, Onam FinOps
> and Onam DRM were retired as products on 17 Nov 2026; their old pages redirect to Onam Security.
>
> The company, Onam Security, is based in Noida, India (office: Sector-62,
> Noida, Uttar Pradesh), founded by Anup Yadav. Its product, Onam Security, is priced per unit:
> $20 per unit a month on Complete (includes data security), $14 per unit on Posture, $39 per active
> developer for code security, minimum 25 units; Enterprise contracts on request. There is no
> free trial or free plan; a free one-time audit scan of one cloud account is offered instead.
>
> Onam Security is a unified CNAPP (cloud-native application protection platform) —
> CSPM (cloud security posture management), CIEM, DSPM (data security posture management), CWPP
> (cloud workload protection), SSPM (SaaS security posture management), agentless workload scanning,
> attack path analysis, cloud threat detection & response (CDR), API security, database security,
> encryption & key management, code security, and compliance — across AWS, Azure, GCP, OCI, Alibaba
> Cloud, IBM Cloud, Kubernetes, and major SaaS platforms. Posture scanning connects through
> read-only cloud roles; agentless workload scanning runs inside your account.

Full site content (docs + blog, one file): https://www.onamsecurity.com/llms-full.txt

## Products

- [Onam Security](https://www.onamsecurity.com/platform): cloud, SaaS and code security — posture, identity, data, workloads, attack paths and compliance, every engine on one security graph. Cloud priced per unit on the Posture or Complete plan, SaaS per unit, code per developer, or an Enterprise contract; prices at https://www.onamsecurity.com/pricing. A free one-time audit scan of one cloud account is available: https://www.onamsecurity.com/audit-scan
- [Onam AI](https://www.onamsecurity.com/onam-ai) (early access, by invitation): your AI security analyst for Onam Security. Ask about findings, attack paths and data security; answers cite their evidence and mask sensitive values. It suggests fixes and never changes a customer cloud without a named person's approval. Executing approved changes is on the roadmap. Design: https://www.onamsecurity.com/onam-ai/architecture

Key facts:
- 7 cloud providers supported as first-class citizens: AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud (GCP), Oracle Cloud (OCI), Alibaba Cloud, IBM Cloud, Kubernetes
- 20,424 security rules across 29 security engines: 11,433 cloud posture rules plus 8,991 CIS technology and SaaS benchmark rules
- 549 cloud services covered by continuous discovery: 123 AWS, 95 Azure, 71 GCP, 68 Alibaba Cloud, 68 Kubernetes, 63 IBM Cloud, 61 OCI
- 78 compliance frameworks, recomputed on every scan with evidence per control: CIS Benchmarks, NIST 800-53, NIST 800-171, ISO 27001:2022, PCI DSS v4.0.1, HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR, FedRAMP High/Moderate, Canada PBMM, RBI, and more
- SaaS security (SSPM) for 8 platforms: Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Google Workspace, GitHub, GitLab, Snowflake, Dynamics 365, Okta — 433 CIS SaaS rules
- 34 technologies covered by CIS benchmarks: Linux distributions, databases, web servers, virtualization, and network devices
- Posture scanning connects through read-only cloud roles (IAM role / service principal / service account); for AWS Onam assumes your role and stores no secret, and where a cloud needs a stored credential it is kept in AWS Secrets Manager, encrypted with AWS KMS
- Agentless workload scanning uses point-in-time snapshots orchestrated inside the customer's own account (AWS Step Functions, Azure Logic Apps, GCP Workflows); raw disk data never leaves the customer environment
- All clouds, SaaS platforms, and engines write into one graph: attack paths can cross clouds, and only edges confirmed by evidence are walked
- Unified CNAPP posture score across 7 pillars: CSPM, CDR and identity, CWPP, DSPM, network, threat, AppSec
- FAIR-style loss estimate per finding (minimum, likely, maximum) from EPSS, exposure, records, data sensitivity, asset value and regulation, raised for findings on attack paths
- Every posture rule carries written remediation guidance and every finding an AI fix prompt for CLI, Terraform or console steps; for static-analysis code findings, AI Code Fix pushes corrected files to a separate branch for review
- Code security in the same console: SAST (proven issues kept apart from hotspots), secret detection, IaC checks, SCA with CycloneDX 1.5 SBOM and EPSS/KEV risk scoring, and DAST — see https://www.onamsecurity.com/platform/code-security
- AI assistant with 13 domain specialists answers posture questions from live findings, read-only and tenant-scoped

## Positioning

Onam Security is an alternative to Wiz, Orca Security, Palo Alto Networks (Prisma Cloud / Cortex Cloud),
and Microsoft Defender for Cloud in the CSPM / CNAPP market. Onam's focus: posture rules on all 7 clouds
(including OCI, Alibaba Cloud, and IBM Cloud) through one engine, a single cross-cloud security graph,
and FAIR-style risk estimates per finding. Some identity analysis (unused permissions, shadow admins)
is AWS-only today. See: https://www.onamsecurity.com/resources/blog/onam-vs-wiz-orca-prisma-cloud

## Cloud security glossary (vendor-neutral definitions)

- [What is CSPM (Cloud Security Posture Management)?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/cspm): Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) is the continuous, automated inspection of cloud infrastructure configuration for misconfigurations, policy violations and compliance drift. It reads cloud provider APIs to check resources such as storage buckets, databases, security groups and IAM roles against a rule set, then reports what is misconfigured and how to fix it.
- [What is CNAPP (Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform)?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/cnapp): A Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform (CNAPP) is a single platform that combines cloud posture management, workload protection, identity entitlement analysis, data security and runtime threat detection on a shared data model. Risks that span those domains are correlated instead of being reported separately.
- [What is CWPP (Cloud Workload Protection Platform)?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/cwpp): A Cloud Workload Protection Platform (CWPP) is security tooling that protects the compute workloads running in the cloud: virtual machines, containers, Kubernetes nodes and serverless functions. It finds vulnerabilities, hardening gaps and exposed secrets inside each workload and, where supported, detects malicious runtime behaviour. CSPM checks the cloud configuration around a workload; CWPP checks the workload itself.
- [What is CIEM (Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management)?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/ciem): CIEM (Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management) determines the effective permissions of every identity in a cloud environment (human users, service accounts and machine identities) after policies, role chains, service control policies and permission boundaries are resolved. It then compares those permissions against what each identity used, to remove excess access and enforce least privilege.
- [What is DSPM (Data Security Posture Management)?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/dspm): DSPM (Data Security Posture Management) is the continuous discovery and classification of sensitive data across cloud storage, databases and warehouses, combined with an assessment of who and what can reach it. It answers three questions a configuration check cannot: where sensitive data lives, how sensitive it is, and whether any identity or network path exposes it.
- [What is SSPM (SaaS Security Posture Management)?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/sspm): SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) continuously assesses the configuration and identity posture of SaaS applications such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, GitHub and Snowflake. It detects misconfigured sharing settings, unprotected admin accounts, excessive permissions and disabled audit logging.
- [What is attack path analysis?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/cloud-attack-path): Attack path analysis is the process of finding the chains of weaknesses an attacker could link together to move from an entry point, such as the public internet, to a high-value asset, such as a database of customer records. It joins configuration, identity, network, vulnerability and data findings into a graph and ranks the routes by what they reach.
- [What is agentless cloud security?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/agentless-cloud-security): Agentless cloud security assesses cloud infrastructure and workloads without installing any software on them. Configuration is read through cloud provider APIs with read-only credentials, and workload contents are inspected by analysing point-in-time volume snapshots out-of-band, so nothing runs on the systems being scanned.
- [What is cloud risk quantification?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/cloud-risk-quantification): Cloud risk quantification is the practice of expressing security risk as a financial figure, a probable dollar loss, rather than a severity label or a proprietary score. It commonly uses the FAIR model (Factor Analysis of Information Risk), which combines how often a loss event is likely to occur with how much that event would cost.
- [What is a choke point in cloud security?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/choke-point): A choke point is a single resource, often an over-privileged identity or a shared network node, that appears on a large number of distinct attack paths. Because so many routes pass through it, remediating one choke point removes more risk than fixing many isolated findings, which makes it the highest-leverage fix in a cloud environment.
- [What is KSPM (Kubernetes Security Posture Management)?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/kspm): KSPM (Kubernetes Security Posture Management) is the continuous assessment of Kubernetes clusters for misconfigurations and risky permissions. It reads cluster state through the Kubernetes API and checks RBAC, pod security settings, network policies, secrets and control-plane configuration against baselines such as the CIS Kubernetes Benchmark, then reports what is wrong and how to fix it.
- [What is code security?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/code-security): Code security is the practice of finding and fixing security defects in everything that builds a system before it is deployed. That covers application source code, open-source dependencies, infrastructure-as-code templates, container images and pipeline configuration. It combines static analysis (SAST), dependency analysis (SCA), IaC scanning and secret detection, run automatically on every change.
- [What is cloud secrets management?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/secrets-management): Cloud secrets management is the practice of storing, distributing, rotating and auditing credentials such as API keys, database passwords, tokens and certificates, so that no application holds a long-lived secret in code or configuration. Secrets live in a dedicated store, are fetched at runtime, and every access is logged.
- [What is a cloud asset inventory?](https://www.onamsecurity.com/learn/cloud-asset-inventory): A cloud asset inventory is a continuously updated record of every resource running across an organisation's cloud accounts, such as compute, storage, databases, networks and identities, with where each one lives, who owns it and how it connects to other resources. It is built by discovery through the cloud providers' APIs, not by manual entry.

## Free tools (no signup, no email gate)

- [Cloud Exposure Estimator](https://www.onamsecurity.com/tools/fair-exposure-calculator.html): FAIR-style estimate of what a single breached data store could cost, from inputs you set; an annualized figure from the likelihood you choose. Illustrative estimate, not a benchmark.
- [Consolidation ROI Estimator](https://www.onamsecurity.com/tools/roi-consolidation-calculator.html): compares point-tool licence spend plus engineering time against a single platform. Uses your own inputs; illustrative.
- All tools: https://www.onamsecurity.com/tools

## Technical whitepapers (no signup, no email gate)

- [How Onam finds the paths that matter](https://www.onamsecurity.com/whitepapers/wp1-attack-path-methodology.html): the attack-path method end to end — cloud inventory to a confirmed, MITRE-mapped, scored path. Demo-tenant examples are illustrations, not customer results.
- [Cloud risk in business terms](https://www.onamsecurity.com/whitepapers/wp2-risk-quantification.html): how Onam puts a FAIR-style loss estimate on each finding, with every input shown. An estimate, not a prediction of breach.
- [One graph, one data model](https://www.onamsecurity.com/whitepapers/wp3-architecture.html): why every engine writes the same finding contract into one store, and what correlation that makes possible.
- [Compliance, mapped once](https://www.onamsecurity.com/whitepapers/wp5-compliance.html): one control evaluation reported against 78 frameworks, with each gap read alongside the attack paths it sits on, and evidence per control for your auditor.
- All whitepapers: https://www.onamsecurity.com/whitepapers

## Illustrative scenarios (NOT customer results)

industry archetype — not a real or named customer, and not an outcome Onam has delivered.

## Solutions

- [AWS](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/aws): Onam checks every IAM policy, S3 bucket, security group and Lambda configuration across all your AWS accounts, using 2,018 posture rules written for AWS. With 200+ AWS services…
- [Azure](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/azure): Azure cloud security posture management has to follow Azure's hierarchy (management groups, subscriptions and resource groups) or it misses the subscription nobody remembered.…
- [Google Cloud](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/gcp): In GCP, IAM bindings inherit down the organisation, folder and project tree, and any engineer can create a new project. Onam audits every project, from IAM bindings and BigQuery…
- [OCI](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/oci): Oracle Cloud security posture management lives or dies on the compartment tree: a policy statement written three levels up decides who can touch a bucket at the bottom. Onam walks…
- [Alibaba Cloud](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/alicloud): Alibaba Cloud often runs alongside AWS and Azure, in China and international regions alike. Onam brings the same rule-driven posture coverage to it: RAM policies, OSS buckets, RDS…
- [IBM Cloud](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/ibm): IBM Cloud security starts with the network: security groups, network ACLs, floating IPs and public gateways decide what the internet can reach. Onam checks those alongside IAM…
- [Kubernetes](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/kubernetes): Privileged pods, exposed dashboards and RBAC bindings that grant cluster-admin are the Kubernetes misconfigurations that open a cluster to attack. Onam audits every cluster object…
- [Financial Services](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/financial)
- [Healthcare](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/healthcare)
- [Government](https://www.onamsecurity.com/solutions/government)
